name: Tonica
caption: A display typeface inspired by halftone printing and the iconic forms of Helvetica.
description:
Tonica is a display typeface born from the intersection of print aesthetics and the iconic, instantly recognizable forms of Helvetica.

Its visual language is inspired by an exaggerated enlargement of the halftone screen: the blurred and imperfect effect produced by this process recalls the texture and imperfections of traditional printing. The typeface was designed on Glyphs using three circular modules — small for the outlines, medium and large for the filled shapes — which were later scaled to generate different weights: enlarged for the bold version and reduced for the light version.

The project is presented through a 64-page specimen that explores the inspiration behind the typeface and includes reflections on contemporary printing history, Helvetica itself, halftone processes, and the intentionally lo-fi aesthetic of the enlarged screen pattern. The specimen largely follows the Swiss graphic style inherited from Tonica’s typographic reference and is entirely monochromatic, a choice that reinforces the visual coherence of the project.

name: Blackcat Society
caption: Identity for a Murder Mystery club inspired by Edgar Allan Poe literary universe.
description:
Designing the identity of a club is different from designing the identity of a company. A club does not sell a product; it brings together people who share a common interest and a common place.

Blackcat Society was born from the world of performance. A collective of actors, set designers, and playwrights came together to create an experience beyond traditional theatre, challenging the idea of a single stage and a fixed, linear narrative. Drawing from literature and tabletop role-playing games, the club reimagines storytelling as non-linear, unpredictable, and participatory. From games, it embraces chance and dynamic characters; from literature, it inherits a fascination with Edgar Allan Poe and the Neo-Gothic tradition, exploring duality, mystery, the macabre, and the blurred boundary between reality and hallucination.

The club hosts immersive events every two months at Villa Zari, an eighteenth-century historic residence near Milan. Its preserved Neo-Gothic architecture and interiors become part of the narrative, transforming the villa into both an authentic stage set and a storytelling device. The visual identity, however, draws from a more modern interpretation of the genre, combining fragmented shapes and flat illustrations reminiscent of Saul Bass.

The Blackcat Society logo takes inspiration from Poe’s The Black Cat. Its two-headed cat symbolizes duality, a recurring theme in Poe’s work and a central element of the club’s narrative: truth and deception, innocence and guilt, reason and irrationality. Each head contradicts the other, creating visual tension. This asymmetry becomes the guiding principle of the identity, connecting the irregular geometry of the symbol with the logotype.

Typography reinforces this direction by pairing Sabotage for headlines, with its fractured forms and deliberately misaligned baseline, and Bastardo Grotesk for body copy, whose subtle distortions preserve the identity’s visual character while ensuring readability.

The visual system is completed by investigative-inspired elements such as redacted documents, rubber stamps, and notes connected with pins and red string. Emotional engagement is equally important, as seen in the invitation package: a red paper envelope, handwritten on the back and sealed with black wax. The themes of discovery and storytelling extend into the digital experience through the newsletter and a website built around scrollytelling.

name: Nook
caption: A service designed to help students living away from home build a sense of belonging in student housing.
description:
Nook originates from a metadesign process that begins with identifying a problem (problem setting) and moves toward solving it (problem solving) through the design of touchpoints and experiences, while also considering possible future scenarios.

More specifically, Nook takes shape as an integrated experience that accompanies students throughout their journey, allowing them to personalize their living space through dedicated kits and renter-friendly furniture. At the same time, it encourages community life through events and workshops, which can be explored and organized via the Nook App.

To do so, we developed a brand identity that celebrates Nook’s values: the hand-drawn logo is a symbol of creativity, the hands are a playful way to represent our mission of help, the different geometric shapes represent inclusivity and the grid is a tool of self expression.

name: World Metro
caption: An interactive visualization of the evolution and global expansion of metro systems.
description:
World Metro is an information design project that translates the Citylines database into an interactive website that visualizes the temporal evolution of metro systems worldwide and their geographical expansion.

The website was designed in Figma and developed in VS Code using p5.js, with the code managed and shared through GitHub.

The overview presents a treemap of all metro systems, organized by continent, alongside a timeline that shows when each system was inaugurated and how it expanded over time.

When accessing the detailed view of a single system, the same timeline allows users to explore the network’s evolution as it dynamically updates in relation to the geographic map. The map exploration is further enriched with interactive tooltips, providing information about each station and line.

Try the website here.

name: Licalbe Steiner
caption: A monographic magazine exploring the work of Lica and Albe Steiner through editorial design and archival research.
description:
On the occasion of the 100th anniversary of the birth of graphic designer Giancarlo Iliprandi, the magazine series Designverso celebrates the work of designers who collaborated with him within the Milanese design scene through a collection of 13 issues. My team worked on the second issue, dedicated to the graphic designers Lica and Albe Steiner.

Starting from the visual and textual materials of the book Licalbe Steiner: grafici partigiani (A. Steiner, 2015), we carried out a process of selection and reorganization to translate its content into the format of a monographic magazine. Alongside the magazine, a mirrored-format booklet traces the connections between the lives and careers of Lica and Albe Steiner and that of Giancarlo Iliprandi.

Within the publication, a smaller-format insert highlights Steiner’s visual identity project for the Coop supermarket chain, framed by red — a color that runs throughout much of their work and becomes the visual thread connecting the entire magazine.

name: BioMI²
caption: A deck of playing cards celebrating Milan’s natural landscapes through Gestalt principles and visual perception.
description:
BioMI², like many Basic Design projects, focuses primarily on the formal and aesthetic aspects of a product — in this case, a deck of playing cards.

Starting from the theme Milan, a sustainable city, each card celebrates a natural place within the city and its surrounding area, ranging from nature reserves to bodies of water. The hierarchy of the four suits is determined by the increasing size of these locations, ordered from the number 2 to the king. The core objective of the project was to design a communicative artifact centered on the principles of Gestalt, form psychology, color use, and visual perception.

name: Bergamo
caption: A high-contrast display typeface exploring expansion and neoclassical typographic influence.
description:
Bergamo Display is a typeface designed in Glyphs, developed from a stylistic exercise: the creation of a high-contrast sans-serif generated through expansion.

Balancing the amount of black was essential to maintain visual coherence in a typeface that blends different stylistic languages, combining the neoclassical influence of Didot with more calligraphic and contemporary forms.

Its thin counters and elegant, complex curves give the typeface a strong personality, making it particularly suitable for large-scale titles and short headings.

name: Nutrizione Aosta
caption: A visual identity for a nutrition practice rooted in clarity, balance, and natural elements.
description:
Nutrizione Aosta is a nutrition practice based in Aosta, Italy, founded by Dr. Silvia Broccali.

The visual identity was developed using a modular grid based on a square and four tangent circles positioned along its outer sides. This underlying structure was used to derive the two initials, S for Silvia and B for Broccali, which are seamlessly combined and softened through rounded terminals.

The upper part of the S subtly evokes the shape of a leaf, creating an immediate visual association with the use of natural and health-conscious ingredients in human nutrition. The colour palette is built around two tones that convey ideas of sustainability, health, and trust: light green and dark blue.

The identity is completed by FF Mark, whose geometric and rounded forms complement the logo, adding clarity while reinforcing the overall visual balance of the system.

name: StudyFlow
caption: An AI-powered web app designed to help students plan, organize, and optimize their study sessions.
description:
StudyFlow is a startup founded by engineering students at the Politecnico di Milano. The project consists of a web app that uses integrated artificial intelligence algorithms to help students plan study and revision sessions based on their calendar, create summaries and concept maps interactively, and organize courses and lectures efficiently.

After identifying the main features requested by the client, we followed the full design process to develop the mockup in Figma, starting from the sitemap and progressing to low- and high-fidelity wireframes.

Before designing the interface, we also analyzed the product’s core values in order to develop a coherent brand identity. The goal was to create a modern, pleasant, and easy-to-use UI that minimizes distractions, supports user focus, and keeps all features easily accessible.
